subtopic: Tensor Core / dtypes and per-architecture support
learningObjective: Understand which Tensor Core dtypes are supported on which NVIDIA architectures and how throughput scales.
stem: Which statement about Tensor Core dtype support across NVIDIA architectures is correct?

options.text: Tensor Cores support only FP16; other 'Tensor Core dtypes' (BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8) are software emulations built on the FP16 hardware path.
All Tensor Core dtypes (FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8) have been supported since Volta; the throughput is identical across all NVIDIA architectures for a given dtype.

Tensor Cores were introduced with Volta (sm_70) supporting FP16 with FP16/FP32 accumulate; Turing (sm_75) added INT8/INT4; Ampere (sm_80) added TF32, BF16, and FP64 Tensor Cores; Hopper (sm_90) added FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) and improved throughput. Not every dtype is on every architecture; kernels must be conditionalized on `__CUDA_ARCH__`.
FP8 Tensor Cores exist on every Ampere GPU; Hopper only added higher clock speeds without introducing new numeric formats to the Tensor Core.

explanation: Tensor Core dtype support has expanded generation-by-generation: Volta (sm_70) — FP16; Turing (sm_75) added INT8 (also INT4/INT1 for research); Ampere (sm_80) added TF32, BF16, and FP64 Tensor Cores; Ada (sm_89) added FP8 for inference; Hopper (sm_90) formalized FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) with new throughput levels; Blackwell adds further dtypes. Because support is version-sensitive, portable kernels must dispatch on `__CUDA_ARCH__` or use CUTLASS-style dispatch. There is no software emulation of BF16/TF32/FP8 on the FP16 path — these are distinct hardware datapaths.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: BF16/TF32/FP8 have their own hardware paths.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: BF16/TF32 arrived with Ampere; FP8 with Ada/Hopper.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: generation-by-generation expansion of TC dtypes.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FP8 is not on Ampere; Hopper added new formats.

assumptions: NVIDIA architecture history through 2025 as documented in whitepapers.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP4 or other exotic formats are absent; new formats continue to be added.
Does not imply throughput ratios are stable across generations.

distractorRationales.A: Wrong claim about emulation on FP16.
distractorRationales.B: Fabricates uniform dtype support across generations.
distractorRationales.D: Wrong claim about FP8 on Ampere.
